headline: The Indonesia long-form is out and running hard: 17,061 views in its first 18 hours, already twice what “Ramayana’s Many Versions” has in ten days. The Ravana long-form is due tomorrow with no long-form draft on disk. The last film Short failed its day-three check.

top3.topic: The Ramayana film in Indonesia: fans dressed as Hindu gods at screenings
top3.signal: In today's headlines from India Today and Gulf News, one day after the Indonesia long-form went up at 938.2 views an hour.
top3.recommendation: No decision slot is free, so this is the one extra worth an hour: cut one Short from the long-form's own opening, Ravana asking for his powers and who grants them, and set the long-form as its Related video. Publish by 19 November while the screenings are in the news. Do not write a new script for it.

top3.topic: Tipu Sultan, 20 November: two days, no Short scripted
top3.signal: The Karnataka row over his legacy is the peg; the radar's step for this week is to record and cut the Short, titled with the searched name “tipu sultan history”.
top3.source: Moments radar, controversy news, owner's note of 15 November
top3.recommendation: Decision 2, in dates: script and record today, publish Friday 20 November an hour or two before 18:00 IST, judge on 23 November. Keep “Tipu Sultan” at the front of the title.

top3.signal: The top-ranked dated moment, six days out; the radar's step is to record and cut the Short, titled with the searched name “guru tegh bahadur history”.
top3.recommendation: Decision 3, in dates: script by 19 November, record by 21, publish the evening of 23 November, judge on 26.

more.topic: Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace, in cinemas 4 December
more.signal: A war film on the radar with no confirmed subject. Its first step opens on 20 November.
more.recommendation: Before 20 November, check what real event, if any, the film is about. A real war with an Indian side and a named enemy makes it the next mass-release peg; fiction means skip it.

skipped.topic: Birsa Munda and Nehru on Wikipedia
skipped.signal: Birsa Munda's Hindi page is at 31.71x its median and Nehru's at 23.9x. Both follow their dates of 15 and 14 November, which have passed.
skipped.recommendation: Skip. The dates are gone and both spikes are the anniversary itself, not a new question. A Birsa Munda film is announced for 2027; that is the time for him.

whats_working: “How Indonesia Became Muslim: The Ramayana Was REWRITTEN” has 17,061 views at 938.2 an hour, with a like rate of 1.9% against 1.0% for “Ramayana’s Many Versions” and 0.9% for the Asia long-form. It is the first of the three Ramayana long-forms whose title states a claim and whose opening names who did what. Day one is mostly subscribers; the reading that counts is day three, 20 November.

The best converter in the 90-day window is still “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, at 11.8 net subscribers per 1,000 views. Its lesson is the shape of the Ravana long-form: “Name the villain, convict him with a document or payment he cannot deny, then end on who is still repeating him today.”

“Why Is Ram Setu Called ADAM'S Bridge?” keeps earning from search: 9,856 views and still several hundred a day on the last day counted, twelve days after release. A Short that answers a searched name keeps working.
whats_wrong: The Ravana long-form has been first on this list for four days and has not started. Probable cause: the Indonesia launch took the week, which was the right call on today's numbers. Test: none needed. It needs a yes or a no today; left alone it lapses on 22 November.

Film reach is still not turning into subscribers. “Why Ravana Kidnapped Sita” brings 0.2 net subscribers per 1,000 views and the Asia long-form 2. Long-form's rate over the 365-day window has fallen out of its usual range to 8.4, and only 41.4% of November's long-form views were engaged views, so part of the fall is how views are now counted. Probable cause: the film videos answer a scene or tour a map, and none names a culprit. Test: the Indonesia long-form names one. On day three compare its net subscribers per 1,000 with the Asia long-form's.

The last film Short failed its day-three check: “Every Ramayana Kept One Rule. The Ramayana Movie BROKE It” has 1,533 views, under the usual for a Short. Probable cause: its title is about the film's rule, not a person or a claim, and the Short before it on Rama in the Constitution fell short the same way. As yesterday's brief set out, the film window is closed for Shorts about the film itself. The Indonesia launch shows it is not closed for a Ramayana claim.

“Ramayana’s Many Versions” stands at 8,426 views and 1.1 net subscribers per 1,000, ten days after release, with an average view of 27.8%. Probable cause, from its post-mortem: “When the hook names a conflict, the next sentence must stay inside it.” Test: at day three, compare the Indonesia long-form's first drop after the opening with the 14 points this one lost at 0:35.

actions.action: Add one line under the pinned comment on “Why Does All of Asia Know the Ramayana?” pointing to the Indonesia long-form, and put the Indonesia long-form on its end screen.
actions.rationale: The Asia long-form is the channel's largest long-form audience, at 154,574 views, and its viewers are the ones most likely to want the sequel.

actions.action: Read the title and thumbnail test on the Indonesia long-form on 20 November, not before. If one pair is still clearly last, stop the test and rerun it with the other two.
actions.rationale: On day one the three pairs were close and the Indonesia-led title was last. Day one is mostly subscribers; the Home-feed audience decides it.

actions.action: Check “Itihasa vs Myth” and “Is Caste Unique to India?” in Studio for visibility history and restrictions.
actions.rationale: They stand at 78 and 255 views two weeks on. Still open.

actions.action: Add the Google Analytics property number to the settings file.
actions.rationale: Without it the brief cannot say how itiha.info is doing, so the website is left out today.

growth.verdict: Needs 226 net subscribers a day. The channel does 41.73/day, so the target is a **5.4x** change in rate. Every lever this channel has demonstrated, pulled at once (scenario "4. Scenario 3 plus one breakout a quarter"), reaches 42.1/day — still 5.4x short. At that ceiling rate 100,000 arrives on 2032-03-25, 5.4 years out.

scenarios.name: 1. Current rate, nothing changes
assumptions: Measured: channel_totals_daily, everything the channel publishes, last 28 days.
Same formats, same cadence, same lane mix.
Includes the channel's one breakout: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" is 1276 of the 2,825 subscribers that 21 fresh long-form videos produced.

scenarios.name: 2. Stop Shorts, same effort into long-form (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 22/day (617 of 1,085 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Measured: 21 long-form and 105 Shorts published in the last 365 days.
ASSUMPTION (not measured): 6 Shorts cost what 1 long-form costs, so the Shorts become 17.5 more long-form videos a year — 38.5 in total.
Measured: MEDIAN 32 subscribers per fresh long-form video. The mean is 135, inflated by one breakout, so the median is the honest number for planned output.
Gives up the 454 subscribers a year the Shorts brought in; they are simply absent from this total.
Below scenario 1 because scenario 1 contains a breakout and this one does not. That is the point, not an error.

scenarios.name: 3. All long-form, all revision lane (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 22/day (617 of 1,085 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 2's cadence, every topic chosen from the revision lane.
Measured on the same fresh set: 8 revision long-form videos, median 58 subscribers, against 32 for fresh long-form overall.
ASSUMPTION: the lane median holds as output scales. It rests on a small number of videos and is the weakest link here.

scenarios.name: 4. Scenario 3 plus one breakout a quarter
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 22/day (617 of 1,085 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 3, plus four videos a year performing like the best video the channel has ever published.
Measured: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" brought 1,276 subscribers on 72,892 views.
ASSUMPTION: a breakout that size can be produced to order, four times a year. The channel has produced one.
